description: About a dozen honeybees carpet the face of the comb, each one no longer than three honeycomb cells across, all of them small clean shapes across the wax.

A hundred or more young bees hang in the air just off the hive's front panel in small widening loops, each shorter than the entrance slot is tall, the whole mass one soft revolving cloud of small dark shapes turning and returning.
Twenty-odd foragers crowd the landing board, each no longer than three honeycomb cells across, all of them small clean shapes filing in and out.
Sixty or more bees move across the wax face of an open frame, each narrower than one wax cap, forming one busy unhurried carpet over capped and uncapped cells alike.

A hundred or more young bees face the hive front and fly small outward loops, each about as long as the frame's top bar is thick, the whole group one slow revolving whirl of small pale bodies hanging in the warm still air.
Fifteen or so bees line the rim of a shallow terracotta saucer of water, each no longer than three honeycomb cells across, all of them small dark shapes along the rim.

About forty bees cross the air above the hive path in a loose busy lane, each barely wider than the gap between two frames, the flow one continuous stream of small dark dashes moving steadily outward and returning laden.
About a dozen bees work a broad flat head of white clover close to the frame edge, each no longer than three honeycomb cells across, all of them small clean shapes across the blossom.
A hundred or more bees carpet three full frames laid open on the grass, each shorter than the entrance slot is tall, the mass one undulating living surface of small bodies over wax.
Twenty-odd foragers arrive and depart the landing board in a steady unhurried flow, each narrower than one wax cap, all of them small clean shapes crossing the worn timber.

About forty bees hang in the air before the hive in a loose drifting orientation flight, each no longer than three honeycomb cells across, the whole group one soft pale cloud of small bodies slowly enlarging their loops in the still air.
Fifteen or so bees gather along a flat wet fieldstone beside the path, each narrower than one wax cap, all of them small dark shapes spread across the stone.
Sixty or more bees cover the comb face of a deep frame, each about as long as the frame's top bar is thick, moving as one slow carpet over the wax.
About a dozen bees work a bank of lavender heads at the garden's edge, each no longer than three honeycomb cells across, all of them small dark shapes across the purple.

A long row of about forty workers lines the landing board with abdomens tipped upward and wings beating, each shorter than the entrance slot is tall, the row one continuous fanning motion, a soft rushing of air out of the hive mouth.

A hundred or more young bees make small widening loops off the front panel in a warm orientation flight, each barely wider than the gap between two frames, the mass one gently revolving drift of small shapes facing the painted timber of the hive.

About forty foragers cross the air in a dense busy lane above the meadow path, each no longer than three honeycomb cells across, the stream one loose moving line of small dark shapes drawn outward into the field and back again without pause.
Twenty-odd bees crowd the landing board as foragers touch down and turn about, each narrower than one wax cap, all of them small clean shapes in motion.
About a dozen bees settle across the comb of a frame leaning against the hive stand, each no longer than three honeycomb cells across, all of them small dark shapes resting on the wax.
Sixty or more bees form a living carpet over a full frame of capped honey, each narrower than one wax cap, the whole surface one slow shifting arrangement.
Fifteen or so bees cluster along the rim of a wide shallow dish on the potting-bench shelf, each about as long as the frame's top bar is thick, all of them small clean shapes around the edge.

A hundred or more young bees fill the air before the hive in a broad orientation whirl, each shorter than the entrance slot is tall, the mass one continuous soft revolving body of small shapes tightening and loosening in the still warm air.

About forty foragers stream through the air above the clover bank, each narrower than one wax cap, moving as one loose unhurried lane of small dark shapes outward from the hive and back, the flow steady and calm.
Twenty-odd bees work the open yellow heads of a patch of dandelion at the path's edge, each no longer than three honeycomb cells across, all of them small shapes across the flowers.

About a dozen bees fan at the hive entrance in a steady row, each shorter than the entrance slot is tall, abdomens raised and wings a transparent blur along the landing board, the row one long gentle motion drawing air steadily through the hive.
About a dozen bees carpet the wax of a frame standing in the rack beside the bench, each one no longer than three honeycomb cells across, all of them small clean shapes.
Fifteen or so bees that came in with the supers crawl slowly up the inside of the window glass, each narrower than one wax cap, all of them small dark shapes on the light.
Twenty-odd bees work the curled sheet of uncapped wax in the tray, each no longer than three honeycomb cells across, all of them one busy unhurried carpet over the wax.
A dozen bees pace the rim of the settling tank, each barely wider than the gap between two frames, all of them small clean shapes strung round the rim.
Thirty or more bees move over the honey pooled on the bench boards, each narrower than one wax cap, all of them a slow unhurried drift of small shapes.
